column1: # What may and may not appear in the public snapshot.
# Two rules, on purpose, and they are NOT the same shape. Please do not
# "unify" them — the asymmetry is the point:
#   docs/**          ALLOW list. Nothing under docs/ ships unless it is
#   everything else  BLOCK list. Ships by default; registered paths do not.
# 1. It encodes a decision that was already made. The author's words were
#    "现有文档放到其它目录下，不入库。文档用我新写的" — that IS an allow
#    list. A deny list would encode the opposite default and then patch it
# 2. The registration cost lands on the rare side. Seven doc files belong in
#    the public repo; internal documents are produced continuously (a
#    decision log, tech-debt entries, audit reports — several this week
#    alone). Make the rare thing cost one line, and the common thing is safe
# 3. This one decides it: the two failure modes are not symmetric.
#      deny list misses one  → an internal document is published. Irreversible.
#      allow list misses one → a document that should be public isn't.
#                              Fixed next time; costs some embarrassment.
#    Between irreversible and embarrassing, always choose embarrassing.
# Outside docs/ the deny list stays, because there the default (ship the code)
# is the correct one and the exceptions are few and named.
#   ALLOW|BLOCK <TAB> path or glob <TAB> 判词 —— why, in one or two sentences
# A BLOCK row is not "this is embarrassing". Write what it actually costs a
# reader to have it, or say plainly that it is executing a decision rather
# than a risk judgement — see the handbook row for an example of the latter.
# ── docs/ allow list — the only things under docs/ that ship ────────────────
